messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the video's camera setup to a rear-view dolly-out shot that moves from upper-body to full-body framing. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the described camera setup and movement, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video. Retain the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, and action in the same environment. Only change how the camera captures the scene.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The character stands with their back to the camera, then begins walking forward down the street.","camera":"A static, eye-level medium shot from directly behind the character.","clothing":"A yellow cable-knit sweater, blue leggings, and red shoes with yellow socks.","hair_color":"Bright blue.","hairstyle":"Hair is pulled up into a high top-knot bun.","identity":"A 3D-rendered character with a slim build, seen from behind, with no visible face.","scene":"A cobblestone street in a European-style town with brick buildings, shop awnings, street lamps, and a Union Jack flag hanging overhead."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The output now shows the character from behind in a street scene, beginning in an upper-body/medium framing and gradually revealing the full body, including blue leggings, yellow socks, and red shoes. The character's blue top-knot, yellow cable-knit sweater, and general action progression are retained, though the face is no longer visible and the environment appears as a different street view from behind the character.
arguments.requested_change: Change the camera to a rear-view dolly-out shot starting from upper-body framing and moving to full-body framing, while preserving the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, action, environment, and action timing.
uncertain: Whether the dolly-out movement is smooth and continuous throughout the clip.
Whether the action timing exactly matches the source video.
unexpected_changes: The environment changed from the original storefront with SOAP and COCOA POWDER signs to a different street with brick buildings, awnings, and a Union Jack flag.
The character's face and expression are no longer visible because the camera is now behind them.
